# Periodic orbits on the regular hyperbolic octagon

  * February 1991
  * Physica D Nonlinear Phenomena 48(1):91-101

DOI:10.1016/0167-2789(91)90053-C

Authors:

Ralf Aurich

  * Ulm University

Eugene Bogomolny

  * University of Paris-Sud

Frank Steiner

  * Ulm University

## Abstract

The length spectrum of closed geodesics on a compact Riemann surface corresponding to a regular octagon on the Poincaré disc is investigated. The general form of the elements of the “octagon group”, a discrete subgroup of SU(1,1)/{+-1}, in terms of 2 × 2 matrices is derived, and the previously conjectured law [R.Aurich and F.Steiner, Physica D32 (1988), 451] for the length of periodic orbits is proved analytically. An algorithm for the multiplicity of geodesics with a given length is developed, which leads to an efficient enumeration of the periodic orbits of this strongly chaotic system.

Armed with precise knowledge of the bottom of the length spectrum of \(B\), we can now prove a good upper bound for the number of eigenvalues in the interval \([1, 3.9]\).

**Proposition 7.4.** *The number of eigenvalues of \(\Delta_B\) in \([1, 3.9]\) is strictly less than 4.*

*Proof.* We apply Lemma 3.2 with \(P\) equal to the set of closed geodesics of length \(\ell_1\), \(\ell_2\), and \(\ell_3\), of which there are 12, 12, and 24 respectively. We use a pair of polynomials \(u\) and \(v\) such that \(u\) has a simple zero the the origin and a double zero at 50.46, \(v\) satisfies \(v(1-1/4)=1\) and has double zeros at 5.62, 11.95, 18.12, and 31.92, and such that \(u(x^2)e^{-x^2/2}\) and \(v(\xi^2)e^{-\xi^2/2}\) are Fourier transforms of each other. That these functions have the correct sign on the required intervals is checked in verify8.sage, which proves that \(\Delta_B\) has at most 3.53617865617108 \(< 4\) eigenvalues in the interval. \(\square\)

Together with the inequality \(m_1(B) > 3\) shown in the previous subsections, this proves that \(m_1(B)=3\) as claimed in Theorem 7.1.

Reimann surfaces with shortest geodesic of maximal length

Article

  * Nov 1993

  * Paul Schmutz

I describe Riemann surfaces of constant curvature –1 with the property that the length of its shortest simple closed geodesic is maximal with respect to an open neighborhood in the corresponding Teichmller space. I give examples of such surfaces. In particular, examples are presented which are modelled upon (Euclidean) polyhedra. This problem is a non-Euclidean analogue of the well known best lattice sphere packing problem.
